1. Identification Strategy
- Primary: Staggered difference-in-differences with dynamic event-time effects. I will estimate the causal impact of hedge fund activism on governance and performance by comparing outcomes at targeted firms before vs. after the public announcement of activism, relative to a set of suitable control firms that are not yet (or never) targeted. To handle staggered treatment timing and heterogeneous effects, I will use estimators robust to negative weighting, such as Sun–Abraham interacted event-time in a two-way fixed effects framework and Callaway–Sant’Anna group-time ATT.
- Complementary: Short-horizon stock return event study around the public announcement to capture the market’s causal assessment of the intervention under semi-strong market efficiency. This isolates very short-run effects and helps validate the direction of causal impacts.

Why appropriate:
- The treatment (activism announcement) is sharply timed and public. DID can leverage within-firm changes at announcement versus comparable firms.
- Dynamic event-time estimators allow me to test for pre-trends and trace the evolution of outcomes post-activism.
- The short-window event study is standard for announcement effects and less exposed to slow-moving confounders.

2. Treatment and Control
- Treatment variable:
  - Treated = 1 for firm-years (or firm-quarters) at and after the first public activism announcement for that firm within the sample window; 0 prior to that. I will focus on the first activism event per firm between 2001–2006 to avoid overlapping treatments; subsequent events are either excluded or handled in a stacked design as robustness.
- Control group:
  - Main control: not-yet-treated firms in the same calendar year (Callaway–Sant’Anna “not-yet-treated” control group), which become treated later but serve as controls until their own event date.
  - Robustness control: matched never-treated firms (2001–2006) using industry (2-digit or Fama–French 12), size, leverage, Tobin’s Q, pre-event ROA growth, and pre-event governance. I will also use “future targets only” as an alternative control.
- Treatment timing / event date:
  - Event date = first public announcement date from filings/news. For annual panels, the cohort year g is year(event_date). For higher frequency (quarter), g is the event quarter. Post = 1 from the first full period after the announcement; a separate indicator will capture the announcement period to avoid mechanical partial exposure.
- (No RDD applies; no running variable/cutoff.)

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
- Parallel trends: In the absence of activism, outcomes at targeted firms would have followed the same trend as controls (conditional on firm and time fixed effects, covariates, industry-specific trends, and selection on observables). Plausible if we match on rich pre-treatment performance and governance and use not-yet-treated controls within the same calendar time.
- No anticipation (or limited): Firms do not meaningfully change governance/performance prior to the public announcement because of private knowledge of impending activism. Rumors may exist but many key governance changes require board processes; we will check leads for anticipatory effects.
- Stable treatment and SUTVA/no spillovers: Activism at one firm does not materially affect outcomes at its close peers that we use as controls in the same period. Industry peer effects may exist; we will check robustness to excluding firms in the same 4-digit NAICS and to using future-target-only controls.
- Event study market efficiency (for short-run returns): In a [-1,+1] to [-5,+5] window, abnormal returns reflect the causal effect of new information about activism; other confounding announcements within the window are rare and/or screened out.

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
- Selection on unobservables/time-varying confounders: Activists target firms with latent improvement potential or impending strategic changes.
  - Mitigation: use not-yet-treated controls; rich matching/weighting on pre-trend outcomes and governance; include firm fixed effects, calendar year FE, and industry-specific linear trends; add event-time leads to test for pre-trends; conduct placebo tests assigning pseudo-event dates to controls; exclude firms with major confounding events (M&A announcement, bankruptcy filing, restatement) within a ±30-day window of activism for short-run returns and within [-1,+1] years for accounting/governance outcomes as a robustness.
- Anticipation/ramp-up: Managers may adjust policies in the months before a likely campaign.
  - Mitigation: estimate dynamic leads up to 3 years pre-event; redefine “post” to start one full period after event; drop cases with news of stake-building or Schedule 13D rumors >30 days pre-announcement; perform robustness using an earlier “treatment” at Schedule 13D filing date if distinct.
- Estimator bias with staggered treatment and heterogeneity:
  - Mitigation: use Sun–Abraham and Callaway–Sant’Anna, not vanilla two-way FE; implement stacked DID as robustness (stack cohorts with clean windows).

5. R Code Outline
Note: Replace file paths with your own filenames/paths. Assumes three CSVs: events.csv (firm_id, event_date, event_type), firm_year.csv (firm_id, year, industry, assets, size, q, leverage, roa, board_indep, ceo_turnover, etc.), daily_returns.csv (firm_id, date, ret, mkt_ret). Code is executable given these structures.

# Packages
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(fixest)           # Sun-Abraham via sunab()
library(did)              # Callaway-Sant'Anna
library(MatchIt)          # Matching robustness
library(stringr)

# 1) Load data
events <- fread("events.csv") %>%
  mutate(event_date = as.Date(event_date))

panel <- fread("firm_year.csv") %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year))

# Keep first activism event per firm within 2001–2006
events_first <- events %>%
  arrange(firm_id, event_date) %>%
  group_by(firm_id) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(year(event_date) >= 2001 & year(event_date) <= 2006) %>%
  mutate(g_cohort = year(event_date))

# Merge cohort year to panel and define never-treated
panel2 <- panel %>%
  left_join(events_first %>% select(firm_id, event_date, g_cohort), by = "firm_id") %>%
  mutate(treated = if_else(!is.na(g_cohort) & year >= g_cohort, 1L, 0L),
         ever_treated = if_else(!is.na(g_cohort), 1L, 0L),
         # Sun-Abraham: cohort year; use 0 for never-treated
         g_sa = if_else(is.na(g_cohort), 0L, g_cohort)) %>%
  # Basic controls
  mutate(ln_assets = log(pmax(assets, 1)),
         industry = as.factor(industry))

# Optional: restrict to support (common pre-period) and drop firms with <2 pre years
pre_counts <- panel2 %>%
  group_by(firm_id) %>%
  summarize(pre_years = sum(year < g_cohort, na.rm = TRUE))
panel3 <- panel2 %>%
  left_join(pre_counts, by = "firm_id") %>%
  filter(is.na(g_cohort) | pre_years >= 2)

# 2) Main outcome: ROA example with Sun–Abraham dynamic DID
# Event-time window: cap leads/lags to avoid noisy tails (e.g., [-3, +5])
panel3 <- panel3 %>%
  mutate()

# Estimate with firm and year FE, clustered by firm
m_roa_sa <- feols(roa ~ sunab(g_sa, year, ref.p = -1, max.lead = 3, max.lag = 5) +
                    q + leverage + ln_assets |
                    firm_id + year,
                  data = panel3,
                  cluster = ~ firm_id)

etable(m_roa_sa, keep = "sunab::", dict = c("sunab" = "ET"))

# Test for pre-trends: are all leads jointly zero?
wald(m_roa_sa, keep = "sunab\\(.*Lead")  # adjust regex per fixest version
# Alternatively identify leads using names
lead_coefs <- coef(m_roa_sa)[str_detect(names(coef(m_roa_sa)), "lead")]
vcov_mat <- vcov(m_roa_sa)
# joint Wald test (if needed, use car::linearHypothesis with model matrix)

# 3) Callaway–Sant’Anna as robustness (not-yet-treated controls)
# Prepare balanced identifiers
cs_data <- panel3 %>%
  mutate(id = as.integer(as.factor(firm_id))) %>%
  arrange(id, year)

att <- att_gt(yname = "roa",
              tname = "year",
              idname = "id",
              gname = "g_cohort",      # NA or year; did::att_gt treats never-treated as 0/NA
              xformla = ~ q + leverage + ln_assets,
              data = as.data.frame(cs_data),
              control_group = "notyettreated",
              panel = TRUE,
              clustervars = "id")

# Aggregate ATT over event time and overall
dyn <- aggte(att, type = "dynamic")
overall <- aggte(att, type = "simple")
summary(dyn)
summary(overall)

# 4) Governance outcomes example: board independence
m_board_sa <- feols(board_indep ~ sunab(g_sa, year, ref.p = -1, max.lead = 3, max.lag = 5) +
                      q + leverage + ln_assets |
                      firm_id + year,
                    data = panel3,
                    cluster = ~ firm_id)
etable(m_board_sa, keep = "sunab::")

# 5) Short-run event study: market-adjusted CAR [-1, +1]
rets <- fread("daily_returns.csv") %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date))
ev <- events_first %>% select(firm_id, event_date)

# Build event windows
window <- rets %>%
  inner_join(ev, by = "firm_id") %>%
  filter(date >= (event_date - 1) & date <= (event_date + 1)) %>%
  mutate(abret = ret - mkt_ret)

car <- window %>%
  group_by(firm_id, event_date) %>%
  summarize(CAR_m1_p1 = sum(abret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Average CAR and t-test clustered by firm
car_model <- feols(CAR_m1_p1 ~ 1, data = car, cluster = ~ firm_id)
summary(car_model)  # intercept is mean CAR

# 6) Matching robustness: pre-match treated to never-treated
# Use characteristics measured at t = g_cohort - 1 for treated and same year for controls
# Construct year-specific covariates
pre_cov <- panel3 %>%
  group_by(firm_id) %>%
  mutate(pre_year = if_else(ever_treated == 1, g_cohort - 1L, year)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(year == pre_year) %>%
  select(firm_id, year, industry, size, q, leverage, roa, board_indep) %>%
  rename(match_year = year)

treated_ids <- unique(events_first$firm_id)
match_df <- pre_cov %>%
  mutate(treat = if_else(firm_id %in% treated_ids, 1, 0))

# Coarsened exact match on industry and year, nearest neighbor on size/q/leverage/roa
m.out <- matchit(treat ~ size + q + leverage + roa + board_indep + factor(industry),
                 data = match_df, method = "nearest", ratio = 3)
matched_ids <- match.data(m.out) %>% pull(firm_id)

panel_matched <- panel3 %>%
  filter(firm_id %in% matched_ids)

m_roa_sa_matched <- feols(roa ~ sunab(g_sa, year, ref.p = -1, max.lead = 3, max.lag = 5) +
                            q + leverage + ln_assets |
                            firm_id + year,
                          data = panel_matched,
                          cluster = ~ firm_id)
etable(m_roa_sa, m_roa_sa_matched, keep = "sunab::", legend = TRUE)

# 7) Placebo test: assign pseudo-event years to a sample of never-treated
set.seed(123)
never <- panel3 %>% filter(ever_treated == 0) %>%
  group_by(firm_id) %>% summarize(miny = min(year), maxy = max(year)) %>%
  mutate(fake_g = sample(miny + 2:pmax(miny + 2, maxy - 2), size = n(), replace = TRUE))
panel_placebo <- panel3 %>%
  left_join(never %>% select(firm_id, fake_g), by = "firm_id") %>%
  mutate(g_fake = if_else(ever_treated == 0, fake_g, NA_integer_),
         g_fake_sa = if_else(is.na(g_fake), 0L, g_fake))
m_placebo <- feols(roa ~ sunab(g_fake_sa, year, ref.p = -1, max.lead = 3, max.lag = 5) |
                     firm_id + year,
                   data = panel_placebo %>% filter(ever_treated == 0),
                   cluster = ~ firm_id)
etable(m_placebo, keep = "sunab::")

6. Expected Results
- Short-run market reaction: positive abnormal returns on announcement. Prior: mean CAR[-1,+1] around +3% to +7% depending on the intensity/nature of activism (governance vs. capital return vs. M&A agenda).
- Governance outcomes: increases in board independence and higher probability of CEO turnover within 1–2 years post-event; greater likelihood of board refreshment and committee changes.
- Operating/performance outcomes (2–3 years): modest improvements consistent with governance discipline and resource reallocation. Prior magnitudes: ROA +0.5 to +1.0 percentage points; Tobin’s Q +0.1–0.2; payout increases (dividends/repurchases) and capex may decline if activism targets capital discipline.
- Dynamics: effects build over 1–3 years post; limited or no pre-trends if design is valid.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID with dynamic treatment)
- C1: Credible counterfactual (parallel trends supported by pre-trends tests and rich controls): 0.8
- C2: Correct timing/no anticipation (validated via leads and clean-window screening): 0.7
- C3: No interference/spillovers (checked by excluding close peers and using future-only controls): 0.7
- C4: Estimator appropriateness for staggered adoption/heterogeneous effects (Sun–Abraham and C–S used): 1.0
- C5: Outcome measurement and clean windows (screen confounding events; robust to alternative outcomes and samples): 0.8

Notes on implementation details
- Cluster standard errors at the firm level; two-way clustering by firm and calendar year can be added in fixest (vcov = ~ firm_id + year).
- Include industry-specific linear trends as a robustness to absorb differential industry dynamics.
- Handle multiple events by keeping first event per firm; as robustness, use stacked DID by cohort with symmetric windows to incorporate subsequent events without contamination.
- For governance measures observed annually, align event time to fiscal-year ends and treat partial-year exposure carefully (e.g., exclude the event fiscal year or include a separate “event-year” indicator).
